VAL-HOST-009.observed: Three separate occupant reservations, each probed with POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations/:id/assign and overbook:false. Case 1 (locked occupant): R1a 76EAHA (rsv_b26225a2-fa68-4f63-b2b2-9c3e9c96c550) locked on G15-T1 at 2026-10-27 19:00; prober R2a W52K98 (rsv_8904157d-...) on G15-T2 -> HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict {"error":"locked_table_conflict","message":"Cannot displace reservation 76EAHA (locked, seated, or within freeze window)"}; sqlite after: R1a occupancy occ_65ee0132 on T1 active=1 overbook=0 unchanged, R1a assignment=locked version=1, R2a still on T2 version=1. Case 2 (arrived occupant): R1b KZJ6TE (rsv_d72ddafb-...) soft then POST /status arrived on G15-T3; prober R2b Z6RVX7 (rsv_68887237-...) on G15-T4 -> 409 locked_table_conflict; R1b occupancy occ_265d74c4 on T3 active=1 overbook=0 unchanged, R1b still arrived soft, R2b still on T4 v1. Case 3 (freeze_min): R1c K29HSW (rsv_d2f40ed3-...) soft booked on G15-T5 with start_at 21:15 local = now+18.1 min (live freeze_min=30), prober R2c 9UPJ8C (rsv_cc7f951b-...) on G15-T6 -> 409 locked_table_conflict; R1c occupancy occ_fc3d6983 on T5 active=1 overbook=0 unchanged, R1c soft booked v1, R2c still on T6 v1; a second probe at delta 16 min also returned HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict. Each occupant satisfies exactly one hard-lock condition (locked / arrived / inside freeze_min), so all three refusals are attributable to the intended condition and the occupants' rsv_table_occupancies and rsv_reservations rows were untouched in every case.
VAL-HOST-009.notes: The contract's evidence line names rsv_reservation_tables and locked_assignment; no rsv_reservation_tables table exists and the implemented columns are rsv_table_occupancies + rsv_reservations.assignment ('soft'|'locked'), so verification used those real columns. The three 409s share one message string that does not say which condition fired; disambiguation is by construction (each occupant satisfies exactly one condition) plus before/after sqlite rows. The freeze case necessarily ran on today's business date (2026-10-16) on the group's own G15-T5/T6, because freeze_min is relative to now; the owned date 2026-10-27 was used for cases 1-2 and VAL-HOST-010. Tables used: G15-T1..G15-T6 (ids in VAL-HOST-009-summary.txt).

Prober P C6PWTQ (rsv_bd8cffbf-b73e-4ff9-b81e-0394645c0158) soft on G15-T8. overbook:false -> HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict {"error":"locked_table_conflict","message":"Cannot displace reservation WEPXWK (locked, seated, or within freeze window)"}; nothing changed: P stayed on T8 version=1 soft overbooked=0, L1-L3 occupancies unchanged, no audit row for P, global rsv_audit_log count 124 -> 124. PII: the changes payload contains only reason + tableIds; a scan for the guest name 'G15 Overbook Prober', phone +15555551524 and '@' found no match; the guest name/phone live only in rsv_guests (gst_11e8f57f-...).
VAL-HOST-010.notes: 'Every compatible table in the area' = the 3 tables of G15-Overbook, all locked-filled; the prober's home table G15-T8 sits in the separate G15-Area so the fill set is unambiguous. Global audit counts drift because other validators write concurrently, so the P-scoped rows (entity_id=P has exactly 1 audit row) are the evidence.

VAL-HOST-019.observed: Raw payloads against /operator/reservations/setup/sections/layouts. Layout G15-Layout (secl_1f7ded26-996b-4331-99ca-3ab921b16896) created 201 with sections A{G15-T1,G15-T2} and B{G15-T3}. PUT placing G15-T1 in both A and B -> HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict {"error":"table_in_multiple_sections","message":"Table tbl_b2e8c3a2-... is assigned to multiple sections in the same layout"}; sqlite after shows the failed write rolled back (rows still A{T1,T2}, B{T3}). POST with the same table in two sections -> 409 same error and no G15-Layout-Dup layout row created (count 0). PUT with G15-T1 listed twice inside one section -> HTTP 200 with that section deduplicated to [G15-T1]; rsv_section_tables holds exactly one row per (layout_id, table_id). Global check: 0 duplicate (layout_id, table_id) pairs in rsv_section_tables; the unique index uniq_rsv_section_tables_layout_table (layout_id, table_id) is present.
VAL-HOST-019.notes: The contract allows 400/409 or deduplication; the implementation rejects a table placed in two different sections with 409 table_in_multiple_sections and deduplicates repeated ids within a single section. The UI-side duplicate-selection behavior was not tested (curl-only group, no browser).

friction.description: Validation contract and architecture refer to rsv_reservation_tables and locked_assignment, but no rsv_reservation_tables table exists; the implemented mechanism is rsv_table_occupancies plus rsv_reservations.assignment ('soft'|'locked').
friction.resolution: Mapped the contract vocabulary onto the real columns and verified every DB effect against rsv_table_occupancies and rsv_reservations.assignment.

friction.description: The 409 for all three hard-lock conditions shares one message string ('Cannot displace reservation <code> (locked, seated, or within freeze window)'), so the response does not identify which condition refused the assign.
friction.resolution: Constructed each occupant so exactly one hard-lock condition applies (locked / arrived / inside freeze_min) and verified before/after sqlite rows per case.

friction.description: VAL-HOST-009's freeze_min case cannot use the group's owned business date 2026-10-27, because freeze_min is relative to now and the occupant must start within 30 minutes of the current time.
friction.resolution: Ran the freeze case on today's business date 2026-10-16 (start = now+18 min) using the group's own G15-T5/G15-T6 tables; the owned date stayed reserved for the other cases and other validators' rows were untouched.
